q: In the parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector, what did the Pharisee thank God for?
a: That he was not like other men—swindlers, evildoers, adulterers

q: In Jesus' story, what good things did the Pharisee tell God he did?
a: He fasted twice a week and gave a tenth

q: When the ruler called Him "Good Teacher," what did Jesus say about who is good?
a: No one is good except God alone

q: In Luke 18, when Jesus took the Twelve aside and said they were going up to Jerusalem, what did He say would be fulfilled?
a: Everything the prophets have written about the Son of Man

q: In Luke 18, after Jesus told the Twelve what would happen to Him in Jerusalem, how did the disciples respond to His words?
a: They did not understand; the meaning was hidden from them

q: What did Zacchaeus promise to do after Jesus came to his house?
a: Give half his possessions to the poor and repay fourfold anyone he had cheated

q: Near Jerusalem, Jesus told a parable about a man of noble birth who went to a distant country to claim a kingship and gave ten servants each a mina. What is this parable called?
a: The parable of the Minas

q: What does the parable of the Minas show us that we should do?
a: That we should work for Christ

q: What is the right use of property?
a: Use as God's stewards; supply bodily and spiritual needs for ourselves and dependents; help others' bodily and spiritual needs.

q: In Jesus' parable in Luke 19, before the man of noble birth went to a distant country to claim his kingship, how many of his servants did he call?
a: Ten servants

q: In the parable of the ten minas, what message did the nobleman's subjects send after him?
a: “We do not want this man to rule over us.”

q: In the parable of the ten minas, what reward did the first servant receive after his one mina produced ten more minas?
a: Authority over ten cities

q: Why did Jesus say trouble would come to Jerusalem?
a: They missed God's visit to them

q: What did Jesus say Jerusalem's enemies would one day do to the city?
a: Surround it on every side

q: Who came to hear Jesus as he was teaching in the temple?
a: The common people

q: In Luke 20, when the chief priests, scribes, and elders came up to Jesus in the temple courts, what was Jesus doing?
a: Teaching the people and proclaiming the gospel

q: In Luke 20, after the religious leaders answered that they did not know where John's baptism was from, how did Jesus respond to them?
a: He said He would not tell them His authority

q: When the people heard Jesus' parable of the wicked tenants and its ending, how did they respond?
a: “May such a thing never happen!”

q: In Luke 20, what did Jesus say would happen to the one on whom the stone falls?
a: He will be crushed

q: In Luke 20, why did the scribes and chief priests not arrest Jesus right away after he spoke the parable against them?
a: They were afraid of the people

q: In Luke 20, the Sadducees said Moses wrote that if a man's brother dies leaving a wife but no children, what is the man to do?
a: Marry his brother's widow and raise up offspring for him

q: When Jesus answered the Sadducees about the resurrection, what did He say about marriage for those worthy to share in the age to come?
a: They will neither marry nor be given in marriage

q: After Jesus answered the Sadducees about the resurrection, how did some of the scribes respond to Him?
a: They told Him He had spoken well

q: In Luke 20, after warning His disciples to beware of the scribes, what did Jesus say these men will receive?
a: Greater condemnation

q: In Jesus' warning in Luke 20, what did He say the scribes do for a show?
a: They make lengthy prayers

q: When Jesus praised the poor widow at the temple treasury in Luke 21, what did He say the rich people had given their gifts out of?
a: Their surplus

q: In Jesus' teaching about the temple's destruction in Luke 21, what two claims did He say many who come in His name would make?
a: “I am He,” and “The time is near.”

q: In Luke 21, when Jesus told His disciples they would hear of wars and rebellions, what did He say about the end?
a: The end is not imminent.

q: In Jesus' teaching in Luke 21 about persecution, what did He say persecution would give His followers an opportunity to do?
a: Serve as witnesses

q: In Luke 21, what did Jesus promise to give His followers when they were brought before kings and governors, so that no adversary could resist or contradict them?
a: Speech and wisdom

q: In Jesus' words in Luke 21, what will not perish, even though some of His followers will be put to death?
a: A hair of their head

q: In Luke 21, what sign does Jesus say will tell His disciples that the desolation of Jerusalem is near?
a: Jerusalem surrounded by armies

q: In Jesus' teaching about Jerusalem's destruction in Luke 21, what will happen to Jerusalem until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled?
a: It will be trodden down by the Gentiles

q: Who will see Christ when He comes again in His glory?
a: All people on earth will see Him coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

q: In the parable Jesus told in Luke 21, what does He tell His disciples to look at along with the fig tree?
a: All the trees

q: In Luke 21, when Jesus' disciples see "these things" happening, as with leaves sprouting on a fig tree, what does Jesus say is near?
a: The kingdom of God

q: In Luke 22, which feast, called the Passover, was approaching when the chief priests and scribes were looking for a way to put Jesus to death?
a: The Feast of Unleavened Bread

q: Which two disciples were told by Jesus to go and prepare the Passover meal (the Last Supper)?
a: Peter and John

q: In Luke 22, when Jesus told Peter and John what to say to the owner of the house, what title did He have them use for Him?
a: “The Teacher”

q: In Luke 22:19, what did Jesus say about the bread He broke at the Last Supper?
a: "This is My body, given for you."

q: What should move us to partake of the Lord's Supper often?
a: The command and promise of our Lord; our great need, which is why God invites and promises grace

q: How does the Lord's Supper signify and seal to you that you share in Christ's one sacrifice on the cross and in all His gifts?
a: As surely as I receive bread and cup, so surely Christ was offered for me and nourishes my soul.

q: At the Last Supper, what did Jesus say the cup is?
a: The new covenant in His blood

q: When Jesus says of the cup, "This cup is the new covenant in My blood," what is meant by the new covenant?
a: The new covenant which God made and sealed with the blood of Jesus

q: What argument prompted Jesus to tell his disciples that they would judge the twelve tribes in the kingdom?
a: Disputing who was the greatest disciple

q: In Luke 22, when Jesus warned Simon that Satan had asked to sift the disciples, what did Jesus say Satan wanted to sift them like?
a: Wheat

q: Who did Jesus pray for that his faith would not fail?
a: Simon Peter

q: In Luke 22, after Jesus told His disciples to buy a sword, what did they say they had, and how many?
a: Two swords

q: When Jesus prayed hard in the garden, what did His sweat become like?
a: Drops of blood on the ground

q: In Luke 22, what did the men who blindfolded Jesus keep demanding of Him as they struck Him?
a: “Prophesy! Who hit You?”

q: In Luke 22, when the council led Jesus into their Sanhedrin at daybreak, what did Jesus say would be the Son of Man's position from now on?
a: Seated at the right hand of the power of God

q: In Luke 22, after Jesus replied "You say that I am," what reason did the council give for needing no more testimony?
a: They had heard it for themselves from His own lips

q: What did Jesus answer when the leaders asked if He was the Son of God?
a: "You say that I am."

q: When the council accused Jesus before Pilate in Luke 23, what did they say Jesus was forbidding?
a: Payment of taxes to Caesar

q: Which king mocked and questioned Jesus before sending Him back to Pilate, having long wanted to see a miracle?
a: Herod Antipas

q: Why did Pilate send Jesus to Herod?
a: Jesus was from Galilee, where Herod ruled

q: Who did Pilate send Jesus to after he had interrogated him?
a: Herod

q: After questioning and mocking Jesus, what did Herod do with him?
a: He sent him back to Pilate

q: Why was Herod glad to see Jesus?
a: He hoped to see Jesus do a miracle

q: In Luke 23, for what two crimes had Barabbas been imprisoned?
a: An insurrection in the city, and murder

q: Who was Barabbas?
a: A man jailed for murder

q: How many times did Pilate tell the crowd that Jesus had done nothing wrong?
a: Three times

q: What did Jesus tell the women of Jerusalem who were crying for Him?
a: "Weep for yourselves and your children."

q: Why did Jesus tell the women to cry for themselves and their children?
a: Hard days of trouble were coming

q: Who said, "Jesus, remember me when You come into Your kingdom!" while dying next to Jesus?
a: The repentant thief on the cross

q: When Jesus died, for how long was there darkness over the land?
a: Three hours

q: In Luke 23:46, what did Jesus say in a loud voice just before He breathed His last?
a: “Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit.”

q: In Luke 23, from which Judean town did Joseph, the good and righteous Council member who asked Pilate for the body of Jesus, come?
a: Arimathea

q: In Luke 23, what did the women who had come with Jesus from Galilee do on the Sabbath after His burial?
a: They rested, according to the commandment

q: On the road to which village did the risen Jesus walk and talk with two disciples who did not recognize Him?
a: Emmaus

q: How far was the village of Emmaus from Jerusalem?
a: About seven miles

q: On the road to Emmaus, who asked Jesus whether He was the only visitor to Jerusalem who did not know what had happened?
a: Cleopas

q: Why do you need Christ as a prophet?
a: Because I am ignorant.

q: What is the substance of all the books of the Bible?
a: The great truth that Jesus is the way to salvation for all who believe

q: As they came near the village of Emmaus, what did Jesus seem to do?
a: He seemed to be going farther

q: In Luke 24:34, to whom did the Eleven say the Lord had appeared?
a: To Simon Peter

q: How was Christ's body after His resurrection?
a: It was the same body laid in the grave, marked by nail prints and a wound, but glorified and free from weakness.

q: Judaism divides the Old Testament into three parts, called this in English.
a: Torah, Prophets, Writings

q: According to Luke 24:47-49, in which city did Jesus tell His disciples to remain until they were clothed with power from on high?
a: Jerusalem

q: What did Christ promise His apostles when He assembled them on the fortieth day?
a: The promise of the Father—power from on high.

q: How doth Christ execute the Office of a Prophet?
a: In revealing to us, by his Word and Spirit, the Will of God for our Salvation

q: Why is He called God's only begotten Son, since we also are children of God?
a: Because Christ alone is God's eternal natural Son, while we are children of God by adoption through grace

q: What is the invisible church?
a: The invisible church is the whole number of the elect, that have been, are, or shall be gathered into one under Christ the head.

q: What is that union which the elect have with Christ?
a: God's grace whereby the elect are joined to Christ as head and husband in their effectual calling

q: According to Christian theology and passages like John 1:1, 14 and Colossians 2:9, what natures does Jesus Christ have?
a: He is fully God and fully man.

q: How does Christ have divine nature?
a: He is begotten of the Father from eternity

q: When did Christ ascend into heaven and why did He ascend?
a: Forty days after His resurrection from the Mount of Olives, to finish His work and prepare a place for us

q: In what sense is Christ the Son of God, and how do we know it?
a: He is the Son of God by nature, begotten from eternity, proved by divine power and resurrection

q: What is adoption?
a: An act of God's free grace whereby we are received as sons of God

q: What are the personal properties of the three persons in the Godhead?
a: The Father begets the Son, the Son is begotten of the Father, and the Holy Spirit proceeds from both eternally.

q: When will the work of the Holy Spirit in us be completed?
a: At the last day, when the Holy Spirit will raise up us and all the dead.

q: What is faith in Jesus Christ?
a: A saving grace whereby we receive and rest upon Christ alone for salvation

q: How does the Spirit apply to us the Redemption purchased by Christ?
a: By working Faith in us and thereby uniting us to Christ in our effectual Calling

q: Who are made partakers of redemption through Christ?
a: Those for whom Christ purchased redemption, who are enabled by the Holy Spirit to believe the gospel.

q: What does the Bible say about Christ being both God and man?
a: It says, The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us

q: Why can Jesus Christ help and save us?
a: He is the sinless, almighty God-man who conquers sin, death, and the devil.

q: How do the three Persons of the Holy Trinity share in the work of our salvation?
a: The Father sent His Son to save us; the Son became man and died for us; the Holy Spirit applies redemption through Word and Sacraments

q: What is to be said about the person and nature of Christ?
a: He is both God and man in one person, called the God-man

q: How do we learn that the grace of God is found in Christ?
a: We learn this through the enlightenment of the Holy Spirit

q: How many chief doctrines are contained in Holy Scripture?
a: Two: the Law and the Gospel

q: When the Jews of Jerusalem sent priests and Levites to ask John the Baptist who he was, what did he openly declare he was not?
a: The Christ

q: When the priests and Levites asked John the Baptist who he was, what did he say?
a: I am not the Christ.

q: Who did John the Baptist say was standing among the people?
a: One they did not know

q: At what place did John the Baptist baptize, where the priests, Levites and Pharisees questioned him?
a: Bethany beyond the Jordan

q: What did some young men do, who had been following John the Baptist?
a: They followed Jesus

q: What does the word "Christ" mean?
a: The Anointed One, the King

q: Why is Jesus called the Christ?
a: Christ means Messiah; He is the Messiah God promised in the Old Testament.

q: What was Simon Peter's father's name?
a: John

q: When Jesus first met Simon (John 1:42), whose son did He call him?
a: John

q: What was the name of Andrew's father?
a: John

q: After Jesus told Philip, "Follow Me," what did Philip do?
a: He told Nathanael about Jesus

q: Which apostle brought Nathanael to meet Jesus, saying "Come and see"?
a: Philip

q: Which man did Jesus describe as "a true Israelite, in whom there is no deceit"?
a: Nathanael

q: Where did Jesus first see Nathanael?
a: Under the fig tree

q: What comfort do you receive from the article about the life everlasting?
a: I already feel eternal joy's beginning in my heart; I will possess perfect blessedness beyond perception and praise God forever.

q: After the wedding at Cana, where did Jesus go down to with His mother, brothers, and disciples?
a: To Capernaum

q: Why can you be assured that the Lord will give you eternal life?
a: Because the Holy Spirit called you by the Gospel and kept you in faith, and Christ promises eternal life to believers.

q: When the Jews demanded a sign from Jesus after He cleansed the temple courts in Jerusalem, how many years did they say the temple had taken to build?
a: Forty-six years

q: To which Jewish sect did Nicodemus belong?
a: Pharisees

q: Which Pharisee visited Jesus by night and was told he must be born again?
a: Nicodemus

q: What is a change of heart called?
a: Regeneration.

q: By what means is the New Birth accomplished?
a: In children by water and Spirit in baptism; in others by the Word of God

q: Why do we call baptism a gracious water of life and a washing of new birth?
a: God's Word and promise are in it, and the Holy Spirit uses it to give new birth

q: Who can change a sinner's heart?
a: The Holy Spirit alone.

q: How does faith justify a sinner in the sight of God?
a: Faith justifies not as good works or faith itself imputed, but as instrument to receive and apply Christ's righteousness
ref: Gal 3:11; Rom 3:28; Rom 4:5; Rom 10:10; John 1:12; Phil 3:9; Gal 2:16

q: What did Jesus tell Nicodemus about anyone who does not believe in God's Son?
a: He is already judged guilty

q: Whose fault is it that some people are lost and condemned?
a: Their own fault.

q: After the Passover in the city, in what land did Jesus and His disciples spend time and baptize?
a: In Judea

q: Where was John the Baptist baptizing people?
a: At Aenon near Salim

q: Whom does God especially love among His creatures?
a: Those whom He has accepted as His children through Baptism and faith in Christ.

q: What does the Bible say happens to someone who turns away from God's Son, Jesus?
a: God's anger stays on him

q: What happens if we do not accept what Christ offers for our salvation?
a: His work is in vain for us; we remain in our sins

q: What does John 3:36 teach?
a: Believers in the Son have eternal life; those who reject the Son will not see life and face God's wrath.

q: What part of the land did Jesus go through on his way to Galilee?
a: Through Samaria

q: After Jesus told the Samaritan woman she had had five husbands, what did she tell the people in her town about Him?
a: He told me everything I ever did

q: How did Jesus say true worshippers should worship God when he was talking to the woman at the well?
a: In spirit and truth

q: How must he be served?
a: In spirit and in truth

q: What does the name Christ signify?
a: The same as Messiah; that is, the Anointed or the Consecrated

q: In John 4, what did Jesus tell his disciples to do to see that the fields were ripe for harvest?
a: Lift up their eyes and look at the fields

q: In John 4, after the Samaritans came to Jesus and asked Him to stay with them, how long did He stay?
a: Two days

q: Where did Jesus go after his visit to Samaria?
a: To Cana where he had made the water wine

q: Who came to see Jesus at Cana?
a: A royal official

q: Where was the royal official's son lying sick?
a: At Capernaum

q: Which man, an invalid for thirty-eight years, did Jesus heal in Jerusalem?
a: The invalid at the pool of Bethesda

q: When Jesus went up to Jerusalem, where the pool called Bethesda was, what was happening there?
a: There was a feast of the Jews

q: How many covered walkways were around the pool of Bethesda?
a: Five

q: Near the Sheep Gate in Jerusalem, at which pool did Jesus speak to a man who had been an invalid for thirty-eight years?
a: The pool of Bethesda

q: How long had the man at the pool of Bethesda been an invalid?
a: Thirty-eight years

q: How will Christ judge those who have died?
a: All the dead will rise again and be brought before Him to be judged.

q: When the Jews began to persecute Him for healing a man on the Sabbath, what did Jesus say to them?
a: "To this very day My Father is at His work, and I too am working."

q: How did the Jews treat Jesus after He healed the man on the Sabbath?
a: They tried to kill Him

q: How should we honor the Son?
a: As we honor God the Father.

q: Who will hear the voice of the Son of God at the resurrection?
a: All the dead in the graves—believers and unbelievers alike.

q: Who are the ones that 'have done good' in the resurrection?
a: Those who believed in Christ, served Him by His grace, and died trusting in Him.

q: In John 5:28-29, who are the ones who 'have done evil' and rise to the resurrection of judgment?
a: Those who rejected their Savior and died in their sins.

q: What does the Third Article teach about the resurrection of the body?
a: At the Last Day, God will raise all the dead and give eternal life to believers in Christ.

q: What difference will there be in the resurrection of the dead?
a: The good rise to the resurrection of life; the evil rise to the resurrection of judgment.

q: In John 5, when Jesus spoke about the testimonies to Him, what did He call John the Baptist?
a: A lamp that burned and gave light

q: In John 5, Jesus said His testimony was more substantial than John's. What did He say testified that the Father had sent Him?
a: The works the Father gave Him to accomplish

q: What does it mean to eat the crucified body of Christ and to drink His shed blood?
a: To accept Christ's suffering and death for forgiveness and be united with His body through the Spirit.

q: Why then does Christ call the bread His body and the cup His blood, or the new covenant in His blood, and why does Paul speak of a participation in the body and blood of Christ?
a: Bread nourishes bodies as His body nourishes souls eternally; by Spirit we truly share in Him and His suffering becomes ours.

q: When Jesus saw the large crowd coming toward Him before feeding the five thousand, which disciple did He ask, "Where can we buy bread for these people to eat?"
a: Philip

q: In John 6, after the people saw the sign of the loaves, what did Jesus do when He realized they were about to make Him king by force?
a: He withdrew again to a mountain by Himself

q: Do people simply make up their minds to become Christians?
a: God must first work in their hearts to attract them, because people are sinful and unwilling for God's rule

q: In which gospel does Jesus state that he is the “Bread of Life?”
a: John

q: What gives the Word of God its saving power?
a: The Holy Spirit, who is always in the Word and gives it power

q: In John 6, after Jesus taught in the synagogue in Capernaum, what did many of His disciples do from that time on?
a: They turned back and no longer walked with Him

q: Who said, "Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life"?
a: Peter

q: What was the name of Judas's father?
a: Simon

q: Why did Jesus avoid traveling in Judea at the beginning of John 7?
a: The Jews there were trying to kill Him

q: Why did Jesus say the world hated Him but could not hate His brothers?
a: He testified that its works are evil

q: When the Jews were amazed at Jesus' teaching in the temple courts, what did Jesus say was the source of His teaching?
a: It comes from Him who sent Me

q: According to Jesus, how can a person know whether His teaching is from God?
a: By desiring to do God's will

q: In John 7, what did some of the people of Jerusalem say they knew about Jesus that made them doubt He was the Christ?
a: They knew where He was from

q: When Jesus cried out in the temple courts, how did He describe the One who sent Him?
a: He who sent Me is true

q: In John 7, why did no one lay a hand on Jesus when some tried to seize Him in the temple courts?
a: His hour had not yet come

q: After hearing the crowd whispering about Jesus, whom did the Pharisees and chief priests send to arrest Him?
a: Officers

q: In John 7, when Jesus said He was going to the One who sent Him, what did the Jews guess He might do among the Greeks?
a: Teach the Greeks

q: In John 7:39, who did Jesus mean when He spoke of streams of living water that believers were later to receive?
a: The Spirit

q: After Jesus spoke at the Feast in Jerusalem, what did some in the crowd say of Him on hearing His words?
a: “This is truly the Prophet.”

q: When the officers returned to the chief priests and Pharisees without arresting Jesus at the Feast, what reason did the officers give?
a: “Never has anyone spoken like this man!”

q: Which woman was caught in adultery and brought before Jesus, who said, "Then neither do I condemn you"?
a: An unnamed woman caught in adultery

q: In John 8, when the scribes and Pharisees brought a woman caught in adultery to Jesus in the temple courts, why did they ask Him what He said about stoning her?
a: To test Him and have a basis for accusing Him

q: The scribes and Pharisees brought Jesus a woman who had broken God's law. What did they say the Law of Moses told them to do to her?
a: Stone her

q: In John 8, when the scribes and Pharisees brought a woman caught in adultery, where did Jesus write with His finger?
a: On the ground

q: What did Jesus say to those who accused the adulteress?
a: Let him who is without sin be the first to cast a stone at her

q: What does the Holy Spirit do in the life of believers after they become Christians?
a: He assures salvation, empowers character development, helps in prayer, gives spiritual gifts, enables witness, opens Scripture, and comforts

q: According to Jesus in John 8, what will happen to those who do not believe that He is He?
a: They will die in their sins

q: How does Christ's ascension into heaven benefit us?
a: Our Advocate in heaven; our flesh there pledges He will take us; Spirit sent enables us to seek heavenly things.

q: Who did Jesus say was the “father of lies”?
a: The devil

q: In John 8, when the Jews accused Jesus of being a Samaritan and having a demon, what did Jesus say he did toward his Father?
a: He honors His Father

q: In John 8, what did Jesus promise would happen to anyone who keeps His word?
a: He will never see death

q: When the Jews said Jesus was not yet fifty years old, what did Jesus declare about Abraham?
a: “Before Abraham was born, I am!”

q: Who was healed by Jesus after He told him, "Go, wash in the Pool of Siloam"?
a: The man born blind

q: After the man who had been blind told his neighbours how he was healed, what did they ask him?
a: "Where is He?"

q: When the neighbours asked where Jesus was, what did the man who had been blind answer?
a: "I do not know."

q: On what day was this blind man made to see?
a: On the Sabbath day

q: When the Pharisees asked the man who had been blind what he said about Jesus, what did he reply?
a: "He is a prophet."

q: In John 9, what had the Jews already determined would happen to anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ?
a: He would be put out of the synagogue

q: In John 9:24, what did the Jews say of Jesus to the man who had been blind?
a: "We know that this man is a sinner."

q: What did Jesus say to this man when he met him afterward?
a: "Do you believe in the Son of Man?"

q: When Jesus told the man who had been born blind, "He is the One speaking with you," how did the man answer?
a: "Lord, I believe."

q: What is justifying faith?
a: Saving grace wrought by Spirit and word; conviction of sin and misery; receiving and resting on Christ and his righteousness for pardon

q: In John 10:7, what did Jesus say He is for the sheep?
a: "I am the gate for the sheep."

q: Why is the Christian Church one despite many denominations?
a: It consists of true believers from all denominations, one flock under one Shepherd, Christ.

q: Whom do all idolaters really serve?
a: They serve the devil, father of lies and lord of hardened sinners

q: What is the final perseverance of the saints?
a: Real Christians will continue in faith to the end and be kept by God's power for salvation

q: What is the relationship between Christ and God the Father?
a: Together with the Father, He is the one true God.

q: Where does Jesus say that He and the Father are one?
a: In John 10:30, He says, 'I and the Father are one.'

q: After leaving Jerusalem, where did Jesus go, according to John 10:40?
a: Back across the Jordan, to where John first baptized

q: When many people came to Jesus beyond the Jordan, what did they say about John the Baptist's words concerning Jesus?
a: Everything John said about Him was true

q: Who is traditionally credited as the author of the Gospel that tells how Jesus raised Lazarus from the dead?
a: John

q: In which village did Jesus raise Lazarus from the dead?
a: Bethany

q: When Jesus heard that Lazarus was sick, what did He do?
a: Stayed where He was for two days

q: The disciple Thomas was also known as Didymus, but what does this name mean?
a: Twin

q: How far was Bethany from Jerusalem?
a: Less than two miles

q: In John 11, who first said to Jesus, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died”?
a: Martha

q: When did Martha say she knew Lazarus would rise again?
a: At the resurrection on the last day

q: What did many of the people do when they saw this mighty work of Jesus?
a: Many believed in Jesus

q: After Jesus raised Lazarus, what did some of the people go and do?
a: Told the Pharisees what Jesus did

q: What did the rulers of the Jews resolve to do?
a: To kill Jesus

q: After the Sanhedrin plotted to kill Him, where did Jesus withdraw with His disciples, to a town near the wilderness?
a: A town called Ephraim

q: What was the name of the woman who anointed Jesus' feet with expensive perfume?
a: Mary of Bethany

q: Why did the chief priests plan to kill Lazarus, according to John 12?
a: Many Jews were deserting them and believing in Jesus because of him

q: In John 12, when did Jesus' disciples come to realize that the Scriptures had been written about His entry on the donkey's colt?
a: After Jesus was glorified

q: In John 12, when some Greeks who had come to worship at the feast wanted to see Jesus, which disciple did they approach first?
a: Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee

q: After the Greeks asked to see Jesus, Jesus said that what had come for the Son of Man to be glorified?
a: The hour

q: When Jesus prayed “Father, glorify Your name!”, how did the crowd standing there react to the voice from heaven?
a: Some said it had thundered; others said an angel had spoken

q: Many of the leaders believed in Jesus. Why did they not confess Him publicly?
a: They were afraid the Pharisees would put them out of the synagogue

q: Which disciple, traditionally identified as the writer of the fourth Gospel, is called 'the disciple whom Jesus loved'?
a: John

q: When Judas had taken the morsel from Jesus at the table, who entered into him?
a: Satan

q: At the table where Jesus said one of them would betray him, what did Jesus say to Judas after giving him the morsel?
a: "What you are about to do, do quickly."

q: In John 13, when Simon Peter asked Jesus where He was going, what did Jesus tell him about following?
a: He could not follow now, but would follow later

q: In John 13, when Peter asked why he could not follow Jesus now, what did Peter say he would do for Jesus?
a: Lay down his life for Him

q: Which apostle asked Jesus, "Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us"?
a: Philip

q: What did Jesus say to Philip that shows He is God?
a: "Anyone who has seen Me has seen the Father."

q: In Jesus' teaching about the true vine in John 15, who is the keeper of the vineyard?
a: His Father

q: In John 15, Jesus says He no longer calls His disciples servants. What does He call them instead, and why?
a: Friends, because He made known everything learned from His Father

q: In John 15, Jesus reminded His disciples of a saying He had spoken to them. What was it?
a: “No servant is greater than his master.”

q: Are any of our sins ever excusable before God?
a: No; we must not excuse them. God never excuses any sin.

q: In John 16, Jesus warns his disciples that people will put them out of a certain place. Out of what will they be put?
a: The synagogues

q: In John 16, why did Jesus tell His disciples that it was for their benefit that He was going away?
a: The Advocate would not come unless He went away

q: What did Jesus say the Holy Spirit would show the world the truth about?
a: Sin, righteousness and judgment

q: How does the Holy Spirit work in lost people to bring them to Christ?
a: He enables understanding of truth, makes them appreciate Jesus's goodness, convicts of sin, righteousness, and judgment, and calls as Savior

q: How does the Holy Spirit call us?
a: By awakening in our hearts a sense of sin and inviting us to accept God's grace

q: How has the Holy Spirit enlightened me?
a: By showing me my lost condition and God's saving mercy, leading me to repentance and faith.

q: In John 16, while the disciples weep and wail, who did Jesus say would be rejoicing?
a: The world

q: In Jesus' teaching to His disciples about grief turning to joy, what did He compare their sorrow to?
a: A woman's pain in childbirth

q: According to the Heidelberg Catechism, what is true faith?
a: Sure knowledge of God's Word and firm confidence that Christ's merits save me by grace

q: For whom did Christ obey and suffer?
a: For those whom the Father had given him.
